name: TerminalView
srcDivergence: Deliberate, not stale — the record's OWN header documents why, and it was read and confirmed before this was written: "The real TerminalView mounts an @xterm/xterm instance imperatively and wires it to a live PTY (session launch, OSC status handlers, resize/jumble nudges, focus/visibility plumbing) — none of that has a design-time appearance of its own; the pixels come from bytes a real backend streams in. This preview vendors only the genuinely VISUAL shell: the banner stack + the themed terminal frame, with the frame's colors lifted verbatim from the real `TERM_THEME` (t…" The pattern is the same across this group: an app-internal module (a spec renderer, a store hook, a JSON-asset-backed catalog) does not resolve in the preview sandbox, so the record vendors the resolvable part and substitutes representative data for the rest. Refreshing from the file would reintroduce the unresolvable import and break the record at mount. Lifted into `srcDivergence` because the reconcile sweep reads THIS field, not a source comment — the reason was already written down, just not where anything looks. Hand-reviewed for `record-src-reconcile`.
